modules.title: How you get better here, and how readiness is proven
modules.need: New people expect to learn by watching and clicking, prepare wrong for spoken proof, read "not yet" as a verdict, and do not know G1 to G4, the angel shift, the eyes-off window, intervals, the recheck or the override path
modules.approach: Discussion; the learner plans their own recall aloud. Retrieval, spacing, interleaving; why proof is talking and doing (Bjork, VS, one line at T0). The challenge route explained. TBRI reviews the gate framing; gate specs and intervals bound (D11)
modules.afterThis: After this, a person can name the gates from first spoken check to release and recheck in order, say what each one asks of them, and plan their own recall for their next shifts aloud. They can explain what a "not yet" means here and what happens after one.
teaches: How learning works here: knowledge at a screen, understanding proven by talking, skill proven by doing at a table; nobody is released by clicking through (teaching style 2; D8)
How to study so it sticks: retrieval, spacing and mixing, with a recall schedule anchored to the learner's next shifts, and planning one's own recall (D15; Bjork, one spoken line)

The gates in order: spoken check covering the full current menu and pairings at depth, practical (drills may be banked, the integrated practical never), angel shift with the mentor as the guardrails coming off, eyes-off window that must include the hardest kind of night, then release that reads "reads still maturing" (D9, D10, D11, D21, D40); intervals, cut scores and night profile are bindings (workflow.*, fact.*, team-gated)

What a "not yet" is: no attempt counter, a required interval and a changed practice plan, safety elements pass in every attempt, and repeated misses open a conversation about fit and other routes, never a verdict (D11; LEA-017)

After release: the standing recheck at every rank including founders, re-proof on every menu change, and a skill counting toward coverage and the on deck reserve only after a real full night (D10, D40, D44; workflow.recheck_cadence)

The challenge route for experienced hires (any Working-level drill or knowledge unit, never a safety element, never the gates of the whole skill) and the override path, which goes to Brandon (D39, D1)
modules.leaves: What ready looks like on a specific node and that node's gate spec (SVC-001). How the map, booking links and content flags work (ORI-002). The drill method itself (ORI-016). Giving and taking notes before the angel shift (CUL-002, CUL-006). The recheck as a practiced rhythm (CUL-023). The leader's side of a not-yet (LEA-016) and of the fit conversation (LEA-017). Why learning is paid and what earns (ORI-022; D6, D41). Contrast and unlearn for experienced hires (ORI-033).
modules.proven: Inside the T0 conversation: the person names the gates in order, explains what a not-yet sets in motion, and plans their own recall for their next shifts aloud.
modules.waitsOn: Nothing to draft the durable part. Gate numbers (intervals, cut scores, what counts as repeated, recheck cadence, hardest-night profile) stay bindings, team-gated (D11, D40). TBRI reviews the gate framing before park.
modules.recommendation: keep: it is the one place the whole gate spine and the not-yet are taught to everyone before contact, and every other gate module leans on it.

modules.title: What ready looks like on your route
modules.need: Learners cannot say what ready looks like per node (runner, back waiter, front server, host; barback, window, well, counter, service well) or which gate comes next
modules.approach: Discussion and a walk through the gate specs, including how a "not yet" is delivered and the changed practice plan (D11). Beverage banks were BEV-011. Needs gate-spec rows per node (D18)
modules.afterThis: After this, a person can say, for their own node, what each gate checks and what passing looks like, name which gate comes next for them, and point to the safety elements that pass in every attempt.
teaches: Reading one's own node's gate spec: the spoken check items, the practical's elements, what the angel shift and eyes-off window watch for, in plain words (D18 gate-spec rows; D10)

Route banks for each node: service (runner, back waiter, front server), host, and beverage (barback, window, well, counter, service well); the beverage bank was BEV-011 (gate specs per node, team-gated)
Which elements on this node are non-compensatory and pass in every attempt, and which drills can be banked toward the practical (D11; SAF-001, SAF-004, BEV-014, SAF-009 where the node carries them)
Where the learner stands on the gate sequence for this node and what lights next, read from the gate record and the sky (D8, D34)
What a changed practice plan looks like for this node's most common misses, so the learner knows how to work after a not-yet (D11; first cohort struggle log, D19)
modules.leaves: The general shape of gates, not-yet, recheck and challenge route (ORI-015). Booking the practical and reading the map (ORI-002). The skills themselves (each route's SVC, BEV and SAF modules). Rating a practical (LEA-002) and delivering a not-yet (LEA-016).
modules.proven: A short conversation before the spoken check: the person walks their own node's gate spec aloud and names their next gate and its safety elements.
modules.waitsOn: Gate-spec rows for each node, signed by the Assessment and Competency Designer (D18), with cut scores and intervals set with the hired leaders (D11, team-gated). Beverage bank content from the head of beverage (people.head_of_beverage).
modules.recommendation: keep: it is the node-specific half that ORI-015 deliberately leaves out, served by route banks rather than separate modules; it drafts only once gate specs exist.

modules.title: Your map and the learning system
modules.need: New people cannot see their route or the disciplines open to them, and do not know how to flag content or book a practical
modules.approach: A walkthrough of the lit next step, the sky and the role thread; an optional prior-craft declaration (music, drawing, languages, science; F P10); AI search as a find tool. tool.map.*, tool.lms.*, founder.unlock_rule
modules.origin: 53 · Tr · F · RT floor, craft (SYS-002 merged)
modules.afterThis: After this, a person can find their next step on the sky, read what each star state means, explain how a star lights and how a module unlocks, and show where a booking link arrives and how to flag content that is wrong.
teaches: The program's shape: the trunk, seven disciplines with four depths defined by capability (Foundation, Working, Deep, Student), and a role as a required set of stars, never a ladder or a height (D3, D28, D32, D33)

Reading the sky: the lit next step, star states (lit, in practice, open, not yet open), recheck due as a house rhythm, released with reads still maturing, held stars, role threads, and the private interest mark (D35; skill web design language 5.2, 5.3)

How things unlock and light: per-module unlock by time, mastery or both, nothing reaching a customer on time alone, and a star lighting only from a recorded gate or proven conversation, updated at close (D2, D8, D34; founder.unlock_rule)
Privacy: a person's own position is theirs alone; the wall map shows structure only; no rankings or sharing, and releases are celebrated in person (D12, D31)

Where the system talks to you: the single-use booking link to a talent block when a module is finished, the reminder when a link sits unbooked, and the content flag on each module's closing page (D13, D16; tool.map.*, tool.lms.*, tool.scheduling.platform, tool.forms.content_flag)
The optional prior-craft declaration (music, drawing, languages, science) and using search to find a unit (system mechanics, prior-craft row; tool binding)
modules.leaves: What the gates are and what a not-yet means (ORI-015). Asking to learn or move into a discipline (ORI-017). The node's own gate spec (SVC-001). Why the house is built this way (ORI-022).
modules.proven: Inside the T0 conversation: the person opens their own page, names their next step and how it lights, and says where a booking link and a content flag live. No separate check.
modules.waitsOn: The live page, the LMS and the scheduling and forms tools (tool.map.*, tool.lms.*, tool.lms.api_access, tool.scheduling.platform, tool.forms.content_flag) and founder.unlock_rule. The durable part can be drafted now; the walkthrough parks as bindings.
modules.recommendation: keep: the program's structure, unlock and privacy rules are real teaching, not just tool steps; the button paths stay bindings and can render as a job aid.

modules.title: Asking for a direction: learning or moving
modules.need: People want a discipline or route but do not say, or do not say whether it is to learn or to move, so support is mismatched
modules.approach: Role-play of the learner's side of the unblock conversation; HighScope plan-do-review applied to one's own learning. Feeds the aggregate read (F P12)
modules.afterThis: After this, a person can tell a leader which discipline or route they want and say plainly whether it is to learn or to move, choose the right way to ask for each, and name the outcomes the conversation can end in.
teaches: Learning versus moving, and why saying which one matters: both are fine, and the answer sets how the house supports you (intake group 2, Brandon's words)

The two crossings: a crossing for learning needs no key and starts from an interest mark; a crossing for a role move is the unblock conversation, booked on a leader's talent block, never something you have to chase (D13; discovery 2.6)

The routes as Brandon described them: runner to back waiter to front server; barback to bartender; host into either team; moves across teams as real but less common; depth in a discipline never requires a role move (intake group 2; D28)

The recorded outcomes of the unblock conversation, including a "not now" with a stated reason and a re-open trigger, and the on deck reserve when the role you want has no space (D13; LEA-006; intake group 2)
Preparing your side: a plan-do-review of your own learning (what you planned, what you did, what you saw), brought to the conversation (HighScope)
modules.leaves: Running the conversation as a leader (LEA-006) and the fit conversation after repeated misses (LEA-017). Reading the map and marking interest (ORI-002). Asking for help in the moment on a shift (ORI-004). The yearly reaffirmation of the chosen direction (CUL-024).
modules.proven: A short role-play of the learner's side of an unblock conversation, rated on whether they named the direction, said learn or move, and brought their plan-do-review.
modules.waitsOn: Nothing to draft. Talent block and booking mechanics stay bindings (workflow.talent_block, tool.scheduling.platform). TBRI on the role-play.
modules.recommendation: keep: it carries a distinction Brandon named himself, it is the learner's half of LEA-006, and it repeats after release, so it does not fold into T0 modules.

modules.title: Learning beside an expert
modules.need: Learners trail by watching and copying, and never ask what the expert noticed or why she waited
modules.approach: Three moves: ask for the cue and the check, name one noticed absence per shift, keep a trailing log. Carrier: the articulation step of cognitive apprenticeship (Collins, Brown and Newman, VS). The learner side of the trailing spec in D21
modules.afterThis: After this, a person can ask an expert for the cue and the check behind a move at a moment that does not touch a customer, name one thing the expert noticed that was absent, and keep a trailing log their mentor can read.
teaches: What trailing is for: getting the expert to say what they noticed and why they waited, not copying what they did (cognitive apprenticeship, the articulation step; Collins, Brown and Newman)
Move one: asking for the cue and the check (what told you to act, how you knew it worked), and when to ask: off the table, never inside a live customer interaction (LEA-001 side-coaching rule)
Move two: naming one noticed absence per shift (what did not happen that should have, or what the expert prevented)
Move three: keeping a trailing log and bringing it to the mentor; the log's medium is a tool binding and nothing is written on a device during service (D8)
What to expect from the mentor: modeling, then coaching, then support fading, and the fact that the mentor also helps judge readiness, with a second rater on any gate they rate (D21)
modules.leaves: The mentor's side of trailing and teaching on the floor (LEA-001; D21 trailing spec). Drilling movements and self-review (ORI-016). How one night works end to end (ORI-021). Giving and taking notes (CUL-002, CUL-006).
modules.proven: Inside the T1 conversation: the person shows one trailing log entry and talks through the cue, the check and the absence they recorded.
modules.waitsOn: Nothing to draft. Log medium is a tool binding; founder.mentor_criteria shapes the mentor side, not this module.
modules.recommendation: keep: it gives the learner a specific way to trail that the mentor modules assume, and it is used on every early shift.

modules.title: Practicing with an AI partner
modules.need: Learners lean on AI for answers or avoid it, and AI practice without feedback can erode skill
modules.approach: Rehearse one scenario, then debrief with a person. Hints, never answers (Bastani 2025, VS); no rehearsal without feedback (counselor preprint, VP abstract; unproven in hospitality). Never on a device during service (D8)
modules.origin: F · RT floor, craft (out of the trunk)
modules.afterThis: After this, a person can set up one rehearsal scenario with an AI partner that gives hints rather than answers, run it off shift, and bring it to a person for a debrief. They can name the uses that are not allowed.
teaches: Hints, never answers: why asking AI for the answer weakens the skill and how to ask it for a hint instead (Bastani 2025)
No rehearsal without feedback: every AI rehearsal ends in a debrief with a person, because practice without feedback can drift (counselor preprint, abstract only; unproven in hospitality)
Where it is allowed: off shift, never on a device during service, never as a rater, and never in place of rehearsal with a person (D4, D8)
Which scenarios suit it (spoken check rehearsal, a role-play line) and which do not, set by the house's AI practice policy (policy, D50; founder.ai_practice_policy)
modules.leaves: Rehearsal with feedback in person (the rehearsal studio; LEA-042). Coaches using an AI co-pilot in preparation (LEA-043). Search as a find tool (ORI-002).
modules.proven: A short conversation after one AI rehearsal: the person shows the scenario, the hints they got, and what the person who debriefed them changed.
modules.waitsOn: The AI practice policy (founder.ai_practice_policy, D50). Parks until it exists.
modules.recommendation: keep: optional and after release, it guards a real risk; hold until the policy exists rather than fold it into a trunk module it would block.
